proposals.title: GZCLP works out today's weight and stage for you
proposals.problem: When you open a GZCLP lift, the app fills in whatever you lifted last time. You have to remember yourself whether to add 5 lbs (last session hit every rep) or, after a missed set, drop to the next stage (T1 goes 5 sets of 3, then 6 of 2, then 10 of 1; T2 goes 3x10, 3x8, 3x6). That is exactly the planning the app was meant to take off your hands.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The app's own record turned GZCLP progression down as separate work: "What GZCLP really wants"; its Revisit-if line says prefill should then come from the next prescribed weight.
The app today: each tier already stores weightIncrement and progressionThreshold, but nothing in src/ reads them (searched at 2426ff4).
wger user asking for automatic progression: "Currently, this has to be done manually by editing the workout program after each exercise."

8 thumbs-up; GZCL lifter wants to know "what exercise, weight, and reps I have to do next" at a glance; their mock-up drops 5x3 to 6x2 at the same weight after missed reps. Shipped by wger as flexible routines in March 2025.

GZCLP lifter on Liftosaur: automatic increments break when the gym's cable stack only moves in 10 lb steps, so "the weight does not increase the next day." Counter-evidence: auto-progression needs per-exercise increments.

proposals.hypothesis: If GZCLP prescribes each lift's next weight, sets and reps from the last session's result (add weight on success, move down a stage on a miss, reset after the last stage), the owner would start a GZCLP day and just follow the numbers, without looking back at last week.
acceptance_criteria: T1: all 5x3 working sets hit -> next session adds the tier's weightIncrement; a missed rep -> same weight at 6x2, then 10x1; a miss at 10x1 -> back to 5x3 at a stated percentage (starting default 85%, labelled as such)
T2: 3x10 -> 3x8 -> 3x6 on misses, then back to 3x10 at a lower weight; T3: weight goes up when the AMRAP set reaches progressionThreshold (25)
The session view shows the prescription and why (for example 'Last time 5x3 at 135 done: +5 lbs'), and the weight and reps boxes prefill from it instead of the last set (record 0016 'Revisit if')
The lifter can override the weight for one session, and set the increment per lift (for example 2.5 lbs, or 10 for a cable stack)
Uses the target reps and AMRAP marks from PR #44 if it has merged; stage and next weight are derived from logged sessions or stored as optional fields, so old sessions stay valid

Unit tests for the progression rules in src/utils/__tests__; a Playwright spec (anonymous mode, e2e/fixtures) that logs a full and a missed T1 session and checks the next session's prescription; no server or sync format change unless a field is stored
proposals.success_signal: Within three weeks of GZCLP sessions the owner starts each lift on the prefilled prescription without checking past workouts, and at least one stage change happens on its own after a missed set.
proposals.strongest_reason_not_to_build: The owner may run GZCLP loosely on purpose (adjusting weights by feel, with ballet in the same week), so hard rules could prescribe wrong numbers they then override every time; and the external demand here comes from other trackers' users, not from the owner.

proposals.title: Show which plates to load for the weight you're about to lift
proposals.problem: Between sets of a barbell lift, the app shows a total like 185 lbs, and you work out in your head, or on the phone's calculator, which plates go on each side of a 45 lb bar. It is a small sum, but it comes up on every warm-up and weight change.

evidence.quote_or_summary: 6 thumbs-up: "I think a plate calculator similar to what Hevy has would be very useful." The request includes a starting weight for the bar or machine.
LiftLog user's three requests start with a plate calculator: "to save having to use phone calculator."
User asks for a configurable bar weight because "its harder to remember what those weigh"; the maintainer closed it as covered by the plate-calculator request.
The app today: a logged set shows only its total weight in lbs; there is no bar weight or plate breakdown anywhere in src/.

proposals.hypothesis: If the log panel shows the plates per side for the current weight of a barbell lift, the owner would load the bar without doing the sum, on every warm-up and weight change.
acceptance_criteria: For exercises marked as barbell (default for GZCLP T1 and T2 lifts; a toggle per exercise), the log panel shows plates per side under the weight box, for example '185 = bar 45 + 45, 25 per side'
Bar weight (default 45 lbs) and available plates (default 45, 35, 25, 10, 5, 2.5) are set once in settings and kept in synced settings
A weight that can't be made with the available plates says so and shows the nearest loadable weights either side
Updates as the weight changes (prefill, +/- steps, typing); bodyweight sets (weight 0) show nothing
Unit tests for the plate breakdown in src/utils/__tests__; a Playwright check in anonymous mode; settings sync is the only touch on the stored format
proposals.success_signal: Over two weeks the owner loads the bar from the on-screen breakdown and stops doing plate sums between sets.
proposals.strongest_reason_not_to_build: Experienced lifters do plate math without thinking, the owner has never asked for it, and the evidence is from one other tracker's users; it saves seconds, not planning.
